title: Why Parents Choose a School
author: Alli Aldis
summary: In this EdChoice research post, Senior Research Assistant Alli Aldis uses the 2026 Schooling in America survey (a nationally representative sample of 1,504 general-population respondents and 2,466 current school parents, fielded March 24 to April 4, 2026) to break down why parents choose different school types. Public school parents rank location and their assigned district highest, alongside socialization with a broad peer group. Private and charter school parents both now rank safety as their top consideration, ahead of academic quality for the first time in years, while diverging on secondary factors like values-based instruction versus location. Homeschooling parents overwhelmingly cite safety, followed by individualized attention. Aldis also examines "push" factors among the 28 percent of parents who report switching their child's school type, finding excessive stress or anxiety, unmet academic needs, and bullying as the leading reasons for leaving a school. She notes that stress and anxiety as a push factor don't map cleanly onto any single "pull" factor that draws parents toward a school, suggesting mental-health-related school dissatisfaction is harder to design for than more visible concerns like safety or academics.
points: Public school parents' top reasons for choosing a school are location and assigned school district, with socialization ranking second.
Both private and charter school parents now rank a safe environment as their #1 reason for choosing a school, surpassing academic quality for the first time in recent years' surveys.
Homeschool parents overwhelmingly cite safety (44 percent) as their top reason, followed by individualized one-on-one attention (27 percent).
Among the 28 percent of parents who report switching their child's school type, the leading 'push' factors are excessive stress/anxiety, unmet academic needs, and bullying.

Aldis notes that stress and anxiety as a reason for leaving a school doesn't map neatly onto any of the top 'pull' factors parents cite when choosing a school, suggesting mental health concerns are harder to design school offerings around.
quotes: Why do parents choose a particular school for their children? It sounds like a simple question, but the reality is more complicated.
First of all, we’re actually looking at two questions in a trench coat.
Both rank a safe environment as their number one reason for choosing a school, followed closely by academic quality.
Safety has gradually climbed the ranks, finally taking the top spot in 2026.
Safety is far and away the number one reason that parents choose homeschooling, and it’s not even close.
Overall, 28 percent of parents say that their child has changed school types. That’s a fairly substantial portion.
The number one reason parents select for their child switching schools is excessive stress or anxiety, with 30 percent choosing it as a top reason.
Interestingly, the top issue of excessive stress and anxiety doesn’t seem to be neatly reflected by any of top reasons that parents choose a school, at least not to my eyes.
